title: Comparing Three Truthiness Policies
description: A table that runs the same test values through Python truthiness, C-style (nonzero numbers only), and Java-style (booleans only) to show where they agree and diverge.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Line 1 defines eleven test values: numbers (0, 1, -3, 0.0, 0.1), strings ("", "false"), an empty list, booleans (False, True), and None.
Lines 3-4 print a header with three columns: Python bool(), C-style (!=0), and Java (bool only), separated by a line of dashes.

The loop iterates each value. Line 6 computes `python_result = bool(v)`  -  Python's rule where zero and empty collections are false, everything else is true. Lines 8-11 compute C-style: only int and float values are checked for non-zero; any other type yields TYPE ERROR.
Line 13 computes Java-style: only actual bool values are allowed; everything else yields TYPE ERROR. This matches Java's requirement that conditions must be boolean expressions.

steps.question: The string `"false"` is non-empty. What does each policy report for it?
steps.answer: Python: True (non-empty string is truthy). C-style: TYPE ERROR (string is not a number). Java-style: TYPE ERROR (string is not a boolean).

steps.description: Line 14 prints the formatted row with the value and the three results, left-aligned in columns.
Run it. The test_values list is created.
The header prints: `Value        Python bool()    C-style (!=0)    Java (bool only)` and the separator line.
First iteration: v = 0. Python bool(0) = False. C-style: 0 is int, bool(0) = False. Java: 0 is not bool, TYPE ERROR. Row prints `0            False            False            TYPE ERROR`.
Next: v = 1. All three see a number/boolean. Python True, C-style True, Java TYPE ERROR. Row: `1            True             True             TYPE ERROR`.
v = -3: Python True, C-style True, Java TYPE ERROR. Row: `-3           True             True             TYPE ERROR`.
v = "" (empty string): Python False, C-style TYPE ERROR, Java TYPE ERROR. Row: `             False            TYPE ERROR       TYPE ERROR`.
v = "false" (non-empty string): Python True, C-style TYPE ERROR, Java TYPE ERROR. Row: `false        True             TYPE ERROR       TYPE ERROR`.
v = [] (empty list): Python False, C-style TYPE ERROR, Java TYPE ERROR. Row: `[]           False            TYPE ERROR       TYPE ERROR`.
v = False: Python False, C-style False (bool is subclass of int, False == 0), Java False. Row: `False        False            False            False`.
v = True: Python True, C-style True, Java True. Row: `True         True             True             True`.
v = None: Python False, C-style TYPE ERROR, Java TYPE ERROR. Row: `None         False            TYPE ERROR       TYPE ERROR`.
v = 0.0: Python False, C-style False, Java TYPE ERROR. Row: `0.0          False            False            TYPE ERROR`.
v = 0.1: Python True, C-style True, Java TYPE ERROR. Row: `0.1          True             True             TYPE ERROR`. The table is complete.
